ai.title: SDK 0.1.2 adds onResponseError handler example
ai.summary: sdk/README.md adds an `onResponseError` callback example to `WebSocketHandler` configuration. `sdk/package.json` bumps version to 0.1.2. Scope limited to SDK docs and package metadata. Example shows async error logging.

eli5.text: The toolkit's helper guide now shows an example of how to catch and log connection errors when something goes wrong during a live chat with the assistant. If you looked at the guide, you'd see a new snippet that prints out the specific error when the assistant's reply fails to come through, alongside the existing tips for handling reconnects. This is available today if you're using the software development kit.

ai.title: Switch base agent template to openai/gpt-5
ai.summary: Backend base agent template default model changed from openrouter_claude_sonnet_4 to openai/gpt-5 in agent-list.ts. base-prompts.ts updated to tighten end_turn usage rules and remove deprecated verification sections. Scope limited to backend/src/templates. No user-facing command or model picker changes.

eli5.text: The internal assistant has quietly switched to a newer reasoning engine when it starts up, so its default helper now runs on a different provider than before. This only affects how the assistant thinks behind the scenes for internal tools and agents; nothing you click, type, or pick in a menu changes. If you were watching the system logs, you'd see the default brain name change from a Claude-based option to gpt-5. It's already live for any internal template that uses the default agent.

ai.title: Refactor gpt-5 model string to constant
ai.summary: Hardcoded 'openai/gpt-5' in agent-list.ts replaced with models.openrouter_gpt5. Constant added to openrouterModels in common/src/constants.ts. Scope covers backend templates and shared constants. Mechanism centralizes model identifier management.

eli5.text: The system that picks which AI model to talk to now uses a saved reference instead of typing the model name in directly. If you looked at the settings screen, nothing would appear different, but the underlying setup is now in one shared place, so changing the model name later only needs to happen once instead of in multiple spots. This is live today and affects anyone starting a chat with the default assistant.

ai.title: Show selected agent at chat start when --agent passed
ai.summary: CLI displays selected agent name after greeting when `--agent` flag used in interactive mode. Calls `getLocalAgentInfo` and `getAgentDisplayName` to resolve name, wrapped in try/catch to suppress errors. Change isolated to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you start a conversation and tell the tool which assistant you want to use, it now quietly prints the assistant's name right after its greeting, so you can confirm you're talking to the right one. Previously, even if you selected a specific assistant, you'd see no indication of which one was actually active. The tool resolves the assistant's friendly name in the background and simply shows it below the welcome message, without interrupting the normal flow. This is live today and only affects the interactive command-line experience.

ai.title: SDK CodebuffClient wires WebSocketHandler and tool-call dispatch
ai.summary: CodebuffClient now instantiates WebSocketHandler and dispatches tool calls via handleToolCall, replacing the deprecated processStream path. New sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts applies patch/file changes with zod validation and mkdir -p semantics. ClientToolName type and overrideTools option expose read_files, write_file, str_replace, run_terminal_command. WebSocketHandler drops hardcoded fingerprintId 'codebuff-sdk' from prompt payload; client generates random fingerprintId instead.

eli5.text: If you write a small program that talks to the assistant, your code now connects through a live two-way channel instead of the older polling method, and it can let the assistant edit your files for you (creating or patching them on disk). Your program can hand the assistant its own custom versions of file-reading, file-writing, search-and-replace, and terminal commands, and each connection now gets a random session name instead of everyone sharing the same one, which reduces clashes when many programs talk at once. The assistant still uses the same underlying engine, but the way your program listens to it and gives it tools to work with got simpler and more secure. These updates are in the just-released SDK version, so you can start using them today.

ai.title: SDK run method supports continuing previous state
ai.summary: The SDK `runNewChat` method is replaced by `run`, which now returns a `RunState` object containing `sessionState` and `toolResults`. This state can be passed back into `run` via the `previousState` parameter to resume execution, enabling multi-turn interactions or recovery. The `agentTemplates` parameter is renamed to `agentConfig`, and a new `maxAgentSteps` option is added to control agent depth. Invalid prompt responses from the server now reject the promise with a validation error instead of silently failing.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, you now get back a summary of where the conversation left off instead of just the reply. That summary is something you can hand back on your next question, and the assistant will pick up right where it stopped rather than starting over. The system also handles broken or incomplete replies from the server by stopping and telling you there was a problem, instead of just going silent. All of this works today.

ai.title: SDK run() handleEvent optional, WebSocket error forwarding
ai.summary: SDK run() handleEvent now optional, typed as PrintModeEvent. WebSocket errors forwarded to onError. Change-file.ts applyPatch import path corrected to relative. Scope: sdk/src/client.ts, sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts.

eli5.text: When you set up a connection between a program and our service, you no longer need to provide a custom instruction for how to display special events; the system now accepts an optional handler for these events on your behalf. If the connection drops due to a network problem, the failure is now properly passed along to your error handler instead of being silently ignored. Additionally, one of our internal tools fixed a broken link to a helper function that was preventing files from being updated correctly.

ai.title: SDK reuses writefile override for strreplace
ai.summary: The SDK now reuses the write_file override for str_replace since both share the same implementation. The str_replace entry was removed from ClientToolName. Error messages corrected to use 'SDK' casing.

eli5.text: When the assistant is asked to replace some text in a file, it now uses the exact same system used for saving whole files, instead of a separate copy of that system. This only matters to developers who build tools that tell the assistant how to read or write files, since it lets them set up one behavior instead of two. The assistant's visible actions stay the same, but its error messages now spell the developer toolkit as 'SDK' instead of 'sdk', so any alert you might see looks a little more consistent.

ai.title: SDK fixes Windows path checks and WebSocket connection state
ai.summary: Updated `sdk/src/client.ts` to use `where` instead of `which` on Windows for binary detection and made `overrideTools` optional via `Partial`. Added `isConnected` guard in `sdk/src/websocket-client.ts` to prevent duplicate connections and ensure `connect()` is called before running prompts. Implemented path traversal check in `sdk/src/tools/change-file.ts` to reject `cwd` containing `../`.

eli5.text: You build apps that use this assistant inside your own software, and the toolkit now behaves more reliably on Windows computers. When the toolkit looks for the assistant's engine on a Windows machine, it now uses the Windows-specific step that Windows actually understands, so finding that engine no longer fails on Windows. The toolkit also lets you leave out some optional pieces when plugging in your own tools, and the file-changing tool now refuses to run when given a path that tries to sneak outside your project folder using parent-directory shortcuts. Finally, the connection that talks to the assistant now checks whether it's already connected before opening another link, which prevents duplicate connections and ensures the link is open before any work starts.

ai.title: SDK forks getFiles into local read-files tool
ai.summary: SDK forks getFiles into sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts, removing dependency on npm-app/src/project-files. client.ts imports local getFiles and passes this.cwd for path resolution. Covers SDK surface. New implementation enforces 1MB file size limit and validates paths against cwd to prevent outside-project reads.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to read files from your project, it now uses a built-in version of that file-reading capability instead of relying on a separate app's code, and you can now set which folder counts as your project's home. The assistant also refuses to read any file over one megabyte in size and will not look outside of your designated project folder, so stray or overly large files will come back with an error placeholder instead of being read.

ai.title: SDK 0.1.3 supports explicit apiKey option
ai.summary: SDK version 0.1.3 adds optional `apiKey` parameter to `CodebuffClient` constructor, allowing explicit key provision alongside `CODEBUFF_API_KEY` env var. README updated to demonstrate simplified `CodebuffClient` usage with direct `apiKey` property instead of complex `WebSocketHandler` configuration. `previousState` parameter renamed to `previousRun` in client methods for clarity.

eli5.text: You can now pass your Codebuff API key to the client directly when you create it, instead of having to set it as an environment variable on your machine first. If you do provide it this way, your machine will also automatically look there as a fallback if a key isn't found in the usual spot. The instructions in the project's guidebook were also rewritten to show this simpler, one-line setup, replacing a long block of configuration code. A parameter used for continuing previous work was also renamed to make its purpose clearer.

ai.title: Move WebSocket error handling from common to npm-app
ai.summary: Refactored `sendAction` error handling. Removed try/catch and exit logic from `common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts`. Moved implementation to `sendActionAndHandleError` helper in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. All action dispatches in `npm-app` now use the local helper.

eli5.text: When the app fails to send an action to the server, it now handles the error closer to where the action is triggered instead of in a shared utility. If you look, you would see the same error message and exit behavior, just moved from a common file to the application's client module. This is a behind-the-scenes reorganization with no change to how errors are reported or how the app exits.

ai.title: Remove onUsageResponse callback from SDK
ai.summary: The `onUsageResponse` callback and associated `usage-response` WebSocket subscription are removed from the SDK client and handler. This cleanup eliminates unused code paths for handling usage metrics within the `CodebuffClient` and `WebSocketHandler`. The change affects `sdk/src/client.ts` and `sdk/src/websocket-client.ts`, simplifying the interface by removing the optional callback definition and its default implementation.

eli5.text: The developer toolkit stopped listening for a behind-the-scenes message that the server used to send about how much you're using the service. If you build tools on top of the toolkit, you no longer need to set up a handler for that message, and the toolkit itself no longer carries the code to react to it. Nothing you see day-to-day changes; it's just one less unused wire the toolkit keeps plugged in.

ai.title: Normal mode reverts to Claude Sonnet 4
ai.summary: The default normal mode agent template now uses models.openrouter_claude_sonnet_4 instead of models.openrouter_gpt5. Base lite mode shifts to models.openrouter_gpt5. The base prompt also removes the strict end_turn tool call requirement, replacing it with a directive to complete all steps before ending the response.

eli5.text: When you start a new normal task, the assistant now uses Claude's Sonnet 4 model by default instead of GPT-5; you wouldn't see it directly, but you might notice the difference in how smoothly it handles your request. The lighter, faster mode now defaults to GPT-5, and the assistant no longer has to signal "I'm done" with a special command at the end of every reply, it just completes the whole task first.
